args.summary: The latest deploy of checkout-api (v2.3.1) failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. In response, the service was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback verification confirms all regions are running v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate has dropped to 0.2%. Next steps: investigate v2.3.1 failure root cause, fix, and redeploy (v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so redeploying it or any new version will require change-manager approval).
args.title: checkout-api health check failure after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary of what I did:

1. **Diagnosed the issue**: checkout-api was running v2.3.1 and unhealthy across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. The deployment history confirmed v2.3.1 was unhealthy in production, and the most recent healthy production release was **v2.3.0**.

2. **Rolled back**: Deployed v2.3.0 to all production regions. Since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production, no change-manager approval was required. Rollback verified successfully.

3. **Verified recovery**: All regions now on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate dropped from 18% to 0.2%.

4. **Opened incident**: Created SEV2 incident **INC-0001** (on-call paged) documenting the health check failures, the rollback action, and recovery verification.

Note: v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so if the team wants to redeploy a fixed version (e.g., v2.3.2), it will require change-manager approval per policy.
